Single Dad Birth Register_Girl With No Name

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Wesley is a successful attorney and decided to fulfil a life long dream of becoming a father, but he was clear he wanted to do this on his own. The fertility clinic took him through all the very expensive procedures and his sperm fertilized an anonymous donors egg and 6 embryos were frozen. Finding a surrogate mom to carry the embryos wasn't as easy, but 6 years later baby J was born. But she remains nameless and identity less nearly a year after her birth no matter what her dedicated dad does, he simply is unable to register her birth because her mothers identity is unknown. South Africa's birth and death registration simply does not recognize that a man can chose to have a child without the mothers identity being known. A woman can have an anonymous sperm donor and register her child's birth but not a man.

Summary:
Wesley Hayes legal career started taking off when he was taken on by the Mandela family in various legal cases, and finally he had the finances to fulfil his dream of becoming a father. He always wanted a child but witnessing the trauma children experience when divorce and custody battles get ugly, he knew he wanted to do this on his own. So at 35 he went through all the psychological, social and medical examinations at the Stellenbosch fertility clinic, chose an egg donor and had six embryos successfully frozen.

He signed a contract with the surrogate mother that she would not have any involvement in the child’s life. She willingly handed over Justine into his arms as soon as she was born. But a month later when the proud father went off to register his baby, he hit a brick wall. Children cannot be registered if the mother’s ID is not on the birth certificate. A single mother can register a birth without the father’s ID but it’s impossible for a father to register his child without the mother’s ID, despite DNA evidence that it is his, and despite there being provision in the Children’s Act that women can be anonymous egg donors, the Birth and Death Registry makes this impossible.


Further information:
So the mother is an anonymous, the surrogate has no genetic or relationship connection to Baby Justine and the Department of Home affairs won’t answer his emails. Now almost a year later the situation is getting desperate. He doesn’t want to put a fake identity of a mother on the registration because it will undermine the status of his child’s ID.
If Wesley were to die, Justine could not inherit from him, she can’t be a beneficiary of any of his insurance policies, or his medical aid. If he were to die, the state could remove her and make her a ward of the state and she would be trapped all her life without an ID. She can’t go to school, he can’t sign for her if she needed a medical procedure, he can’t travel with her. Her constitutional right to have a name and a nationality are being withheld in a country with one of the world’s most progressive constitutions.
The bigger context is that despite South Africa’s progressive Constitution around gender issues, same-sex marriages and adoption by same-sex and single parents, what it boils down to is men are prejudiced against. A case in point is a South African father who has children with a Nigerian woman out of wedlock, and cannot register those children as South African.
Then there are the rights of fathers outside of marriage, an interesting case was the father who kidnapped his baby after she was put up for adoption because as an unmarried father he had no say in what happened to her. There are cases where mothers get custody of children when it’s clear the father is in fact a better parent, there is this cultural belief or norm that women make better parents.
Wesley is going to fight this in the Grahamstown Magistrates’ Court but will take it to the Constitutional Court because men should be able to chose to have children on their own just as women can make that choice and their babies’ certificates are not withheld.
Wesley is keen to do the story and has given us exclusive TV access. He lives on a farm and is crazy about his horses. His aging parents who love an adore their grandchild also live on the farm. He is a great character and the visuals will be good

Extra Budget Items:
Wesley lives in Queenstown and flights to East London are few and far between and unpredictable currently, so we need a travel day on the Monday for Masa to allow for flight cancellations. Cameraman travel from PE to Queenstown of 700 km at R3.50 a KM works out to an additional R2450. I will need a half day with Masa in Pretoria to do interview with Min Aaron Moseoaledi and with Karabo Ozah Director of Centre for Child law who is also in Pretoria. I do not have to be there for those interviews if a researcher from the office can assist/accompany Masa as we did under hard lockdown

Script:


Script: Growing up on a farm in the Eastern Cape, Wesley Hayes always knew he wanted to be a father, but he was clear, it was something he was doing it on his own
Wesley: I couldn't really imagine myself with anybody, and also there would be no bickering with and maintenance issues and custody issues.
Mac “Are you a divorce lawyer”
Wesley I do a fair number of divorces ja so you see with the children being pulled between the parents and being used as a pawn .So initially I thought, .. it was impossible. And then I studied the law and realized it is possible
Script: Wesley runs his own law practice in Komani and started the journey towards fatherhood, 6 years ago. At a fertility clinic he went through numerous tests and then chose an egg from an anonymous donor with the closest possible match to his family genes. Using his sperm they fertilized the eggs and 10 embryos were frozen.
LINK Wesley had to jump through so many hoops just to get the green light to have a child on his own. He has been psychologically, socially and even financially assessed
Script: After going through tests with 7 potential surrogates, all of which fell through for various reasons, Wesley was on the verge of giving up on his dream, when he finally found a surrogate in his hometown
Mac: What is the response from your family and friends
Wesley: Well, I never told anyone. I sort of went on my mission myself. My folks were quite shocked but happy
Script: Sadly, Wesley couldn’t be at her birth because she was born during Covid restrictions, so he waited anxiously on the farm when the surrogate went into labour. The call finally came through at 3 am that Justine, was on the way
Wesley: So when I got there, she'd already been born I immediately recognized I knew she was mine and I just start crying. Wow. I just sat there. I said, I can sit in a chair and take off my shirt and I put it on my chest and I just cried and cried and cried for like an age. Because it had been coming for a long time, you know, and not as real. And there she was. And here, she is.
LINK at DHA “After 6 years of waiting to become a father Wesley pitched up here at the the department of home affairs a month after his daughter’s birth full of excitement to name and register his child.
Wesley: So I took my file down to home affairs and I mean, the cue was just unbelievable. So it was 3 days before I got into home affairs. and immediately the lady said, where's the mother's details? I said, no, there is no mother she was born by surrogate. I'm a single dad., here is the surrogacy agreement, here is the court order. And she said, ayi this can't happen, you know, we can't register without the consent of the mother. There has to be a mother…..And then I realized that the Birth and Death Registries Act doesn't allow me to register as a single father. And then that's when the problem started.
Script: Advocate David Smith, who has taken up Wesleys’ case, discovered that despite the Children’s Act providing for surrogacy and anonymous egg donation, the Birth and Death Registration Act has only 4 categories under which children can be registered.
David: A child born either in or out of wedlock, a child born outside the borders of South Africa, or a child that's an orphan child.
David: The problem here is that Wesley can't go alone to home affairs to register his child's birth. Wesley would need a mother to accompany him to the satisfaction of home affairs. a mother doesn't necessarily have that same problem because a mother can go alone to home affairs without the father.
Wesley: So I couldn't explain to anybody that she was born by a surrogate, put the surrogate name there. And I was like, no. She's relinquished her rights and responsibilities to the child via the surrogacy agreement, which has been made in order of court.
Script: Director for the Centre of Child Law, Karabo Ozah, says same sex couples face similar problems
Karabo , the challenge they face is this Home Affairs tells them that they only recognize one mother the minute you need to, two mothers, they don't know what to do and then Home Affairs said to them that they if they conclude a life partnership agreement, they will add the other mother. But now you are kind of forcing people to comply with requirements that are not even in any law for you to actually register the birth of the child
Script: When Wesley wrote to the Department of Home Affairs the state attorney said he could register Justine if he put “born from surrogacy” under the mother’s details. Karabo advised Wesley not to accept this offer
Karabo, that's problematic because you are labelling the child and also the Children's Act has privacy provisions in relation to where children have been conceived via surrogacy. It gives the power to the parent to disclose when and how surrogates are guaranteed their privacy because they are actually in the court papers they are anonymized
Script: The problem is that the Birth and Deaths registration Act is out of synch with the Constitution and the Children’s Act
Karabo: the problem we have is that our birth and death registration act is actually outdated. So even though we have recognized surrogacy agreements, and people have been doing surrogacy since the Children’s act came into operation, the Birth and Death Registration Act there was never a process of putting provisions there to enable the birth registration of children born through surrogacy agreements
Mac: as a father, you now realize that your baby daughter does not have an id. What is the impact of that and what does that mean?
Wesley: she'd be unable to inherit because she wouldn't be a legal person to inherit from me, um, and she'd be, in essence, become a ward of the state. My parents wouldn't really have a rightful claim to her. And besides that, I can't agree to any urgent surgery should she need surgery. Uh, medical aid is a problem. Insurance is a problem. Just everything, everything, everything that flows from being a registered individual …..besides not having a name and not having a right to nationality and so forth and so on
Mac: What are some of your worst fears around this?
Wesley: My worst fears, me dying, without a doubt. I mean, if I were to die, I mean, you know, who takes care of her I mean, that's that's that's without a doubt the worst fear.
Upsound Grandpa
Script: Having done this whole process on his own, Wesley was surprised to learn recently, that surrogacy attorney Robynne Friedeman, had assisted at least 20 single dads both straight and gay, to register their children.
Robynne: so we have a surrogate motherhood agreement which is entered into between the commissioning parent because we are focusing on a single parent at the moment and the surrogate mother and her husband or partner potentially because he's also involved And then there's a high court application which accompanies that agreement. so We ask the court to confirm our surrogate motherhood agreement. And we also request the court to direct the Department of Home Affairs to register the birth in the name of the single dad
Wesley: I was completely unaware that that was the practice that was taking place. And as an attorney, I cannot see how it is possible to order a department to do something without having cited them as a party to the proceedings.
Mac: Does the Department of Home Affairs have a right of reply? Are these cited in the document? And if you haven't cited them, is that not problematic and you have no issues going forward?
Robynne: never, ever had a judge raise a query with me that we haven't cited the Department of Home Affairs because it follows from the act. The Children's Act specifically states that from the moment of birth of the child, that the child is the child of the commissioning parent or parents.
Script: The Department of Home Affairs says Wesley’s case is not unusual, and they have assisted other fathers to register under section 9 of the Birth and Deaths registration Act. They recently tried to assist Wesley to register his child
David: They have made an offer to leave of the mother's name off completely, but Wesley's intention is that that's not good enough. There must be a provision in the act for children who are born without mothers.
Karabo home affairs kind of response is always to try and say, well, we can accommodate you if we do one, two, three, four. But that discretion is problematic because somebody in Eastern Cape will be treated differently from somebody in Pretoria. You know, it depends on who you get that office helping you, but you must always escalate. So that shows you there's a gap in the law….. The law does need to be amended
Script: As a father, it was tempting to accept the DHA offer, but as a attorney, who acts for the Mandela family, Wesley feels compelled to follow the law, otherwise he thinks it will makes Justine’s ID document open to be challenged in the future
Link: After nearly a year of trying to resolve the problem with the Department of Home Affairs Wesley turned to the courts to try and get his child registered
Wesley: So the application is in two parts part A which we are asking for as an immediate relief, to have her registered, and that the Part B is that she that the law gets amended, that men in future and the same or similar situation to what I am in don't have to go through what we're going through.
Script: The DHA says it’s reviewing its policies and laws to more accurately reflect the realities of our evolving society
Mac: Has it angered you that you'd have to you'd have to go through all of these hoops
Wesley:.Initially, no. But recently, yes it is annoying that I have to do it and it should have been done sort of years ago, I don't know how old the oldest child is that was registered through this way, but that person should have been the first person to have done it.
Script: In a groundbreaking judgement the High Court in Makhanda acknowledged that baby Justine was born of surrogacy to a single dad and instructed the Department of home affairs to register her birth. On her birth certificate Wesley will be reflected as the sole parent and under mother it will read “not applicable”
Wesley Well immediately she is recognised as a person and I am recognised as her father and now she can inherit my horses .I think it's just going to make it a lot easier for people who follow and they don't have to go through the angst that has culminated from it
Script “Next is the High Court challenge on the constitutionality of the birth and death registration act. Both Wesley and Home Affairs will make their submissions. If Wesley is successful, it will go on to the constitutional court

But recently, yes it is annoying that I have to do it and it should have been done sort of years ago, I don't know how old the oldest child is that was registered through this way, but that person should have been the first person to have done it. Script: In a groundbreaking judgement the High Court in Makhanda acknowledged that baby Justine was born of surrogacy to a single dad and instructed the Department of home affairs to register her birth. On her birth certificate Wesley will be reflected as the sole parent and under mother it will read “not applicable” Wesley Well immediately she is recognised as a person and I am recognised as her father and now she can inherit my horses .I think it's just going to make it a lot easier for people who follow and they don't have to go through the angst that has culminated from it Script “Next is the High Court challenge on the constitutionality of the birth and death registration act. Both Wesley and Home Affairs will make their submissions. If Wesley is successful, it will go on to the constitutional court

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Wesley is a successful attorney and decided to fulfil a life long dream of becoming a father, but he was clear he wanted to do this on his own. The fertility clinic took him through all the very expensive procedures and his sperm fertilized an anonymous donors egg and 6 embryos were frozen. Finding a surrogate mom to carry the embryos wasn't as easy, but 6 years later baby J was born. But she remains nameless and identity less nearly a year after her birth no matter what her dedicated dad does, he simply is unable to register her birth because her mothers identity is unknown. South Africa's birth and death registration simply does not recognize that a man can chose to have a child without the mothers identity being known. A woman can have an anonymous sperm donor and register her child's birth but not a man.
metadata.Summary: Wesley Hayes legal career started taking off when he was taken on by the Mandela family in various legal cases, and finally he had the finances to fulfil his dream of becoming a father. He always wanted a child but witnessing the trauma children experience when divorce and custody battles get ugly, he knew he wanted to do this on his own. So at 35 he went through all the psychological, social and medical examinations at the Stellenbosch fertility clinic, chose an egg donor and had six embryos successfully frozen. He signed a contract with the surrogate mother that she would not have any involvement in the child’s life. She willingly handed over Justine into his arms as soon as she was born. But a month later when the proud father went off to register his baby, he hit a brick wall. Children cannot be registered if the mother’s ID is not on the birth certificate. A single mother can register a birth without the father’s ID but it’s impossible for a father to register his child without the mother’s ID, despite DNA evidence that it is his, and despite there being provision in the Children’s Act that women can be anonymous egg donors, the Birth and Death Registry makes this impossible.
metadata.Further information: So the mother is an anonymous, the surrogate has no genetic or relationship connection to Baby Justine and the Department of Home affairs won’t answer his emails. Now almost a year later the situation is getting desperate. He doesn’t want to put a fake identity of a mother on the registration because it will undermine the status of his child’s ID. If Wesley were to die, Justine could not inherit from him, she can’t be a beneficiary of any of his insurance policies, or his medical aid. If he were to die, the state could remove her and make her a ward of the state and she would be trapped all her life without an ID. She can’t go to school, he can’t sign for her if she needed a medical procedure, he can’t travel with her. Her constitutional right to have a name and a nationality are being withheld in a country with one of the world’s most progressive constitutions. The bigger context is that despite South Africa’s progressive Constitution around gender issues, same-sex marriages and adoption by same-sex and single parents, what it boils down to is men are prejudiced against. A case in point is a South African father who has children with a Nigerian woman out of wedlock, and cannot register those children as South African. Then there are the rights of fathers outside of marriage, an interesting case was the father who kidnapped his baby after she was put up for adoption because as an unmarried father he had no say in what happened to her. There are cases where mothers get custody of children when it’s clear the father is in fact a better parent, there is this cultural belief or norm that women make better parents. Wesley is going to fight this in the Grahamstown Magistrates’ Court but will take it to the Constitutional Court because men should be able to chose to have children on their own just as women can make that choice and their babies’ certificates are not withheld. Wesley is keen to do the story and has given us exclusive TV access. He lives on a farm and is crazy about his horses. His aging parents who love an adore their grandchild also live on the farm. He is a great character and the visuals will be good
